feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong senior-level CV with clear positioning in digital communications/strategy and credible progression at NACo. It reads polished and substantive, but it is slightly dense and repetitive, with some missed opportunities to sharpen impact through clearer outcomes and tighter structure.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear professional brand: the headline, summary, and experience consistently support a strong digital strategy/communications leadership profile.  
- Credible career progression: multiple promotions within one organization show trust, growth, and increasing scope.  
- Good use of specifics: Drupal, GA4, BigQuery, 10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, and studio build-out add credibility and impact.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily. Consolidating these sections would improve structure and readability.  
- Add stronger outcome language: several bullets describe responsibilities more than results. Include measurable business/organizational impact where possible.  
- Fix style consistency and minor writing issues: use “12 years of experience” instead of “12 years experience”; standardize serial commas (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia” vs “web, email, social and multimedia”); consider consistent capitalization/hyphenation for terms like “organization-wide,” “member-facing,” and “cross-channel/multi-channel.” No major misspellings or typos found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary that aligns with the CV’s senior digital leadership focus. It would be sharper with a more distinctive opening, tighter phrasing, and a few concrete signals of sector relevance.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years’ experience” for cleaner style and correct grammar.
- Lead with your senior value proposition and public-sector/mission-driven niche, not a generic profession label.
- Replace broad phrases like “web, content, email, social media, and multimedia programs” with “multi-channel digital communications” to reduce listiness.
- Suggested rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years’ experience leading multi-channel programs for mission-driven and public-sector organizations. Brings deep expertise in cross-channel communications, web and platform modernization, and the workflows, governance, and systems that enable complex teams to publish effectively at scale. Strong background in advocacy messaging, stakeholder coordination, and translating technical or policy issues into clear, accessible content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications” and workflow/systems language overlap with Core Competencies; keep the intro high-level.
- Avoid adding tools or platform names here, since those are covered well in skills and experience.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing higher-level leadership strengths will make it more distinctive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic terms with sharper, senior-level language: “Digital transformation strategy” instead of “Digital strategy & transformation,” and “Cross-functional stakeholder leadership” instead of “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination.”
- Group related items to reduce repetition and improve flow: strategy, platforms/workflows, analytics, communications, multimedia.
- Use parallel noun phrases throughout for consistency.
- Suggested rewrite: Digital transformation strategy • Cross-channel communications leadership • Web platform and CMS administration • Editorial workflow and content operations design • Analytics, reporting, and performance insights • Workflow architecture and systems improvement • Cross-functional stakeholder leadership • Policy and advocacy communications • Multimedia and live event production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multi-channel communication” duplicates the header’s “cross-channel communications” and Topline Skills’ “Multi-channel communications leadership.”
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” overlaps with Soft Skills; consider keeping the stronger leadership version in only one place.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear relevance to your headline, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the Recent Projects footer and prior NACo entries. Tighten it around scope, technical leadership, and outcomes.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Embedded as a full-time strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvement, campaign delivery, and content operations.”
- Replace generic verbs (“support,” “advise”) with ownership language: “Led,” “Built,” “Designed,” “Implemented,” “Established.”
- Consolidate bullets around 3 themes: enterprise web/CMS improvement, campaign/microsite delivery in Drupal, and AI-enabled search/content discovery.
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/pages supported, publishers enabled, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, workflow time saved, search accuracy/engagement gains.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “AI-enabled search initiative” and Drupal microsite work duplicate the Recent Projects section; keep this entry higher-level and let the footer hold project specifics.
- “Governance, workflows, analytics” also echoes the 2022–2024 NACo role; emphasize what is new in this consulting engagement.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to foreground enterprise outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management details already covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit
- Open with scope + leadership: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Combine the strongest achievements into sharper, outcome-led bullets: “Led redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page Drupal website, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make impact more explicit where possible: add team size, budget, efficiency gains, reporting adoption, production cost savings, or engagement growth for email/social/video.
- Tighten softer bullets: “Implemented digital governance, publishing standards, and cross-department planning systems to improve consistency and execution.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership and transformation.
- Video studio build may overlap with footer project examples; keep the CV item at strategic level, not production detail.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this item overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager/Producer role. Make it more clearly about executional leadership, editorial systems, and channel growth at this stage.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a tighter scope/result line: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy publishing.”
- Replace “helping” language with direct ownership: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Sharpen the video bullet: “Produced and grew a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one stronger systems bullet: “Built stronger editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, improving coordination and content consistency.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital communications across web, email, social and video” is very similar to the Director role; avoid repeating platform lists unless paired with distinct outcomes.
- Weekly video updates also appear in the 2015–2018 role; frame this here as scaling/formalizing the program, not starting it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this topline skills item overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. It should be tighter, more distinctive, and framed around leadership scope rather than repeating generic phrases.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad labels with sharper, higher-value terms: “Enterprise digital strategy,” “Content governance and editorial operations,” “Cross-channel communications leadership,” “Public-sector and advocacy communications,” “Audience and journey-based content planning”
- Use parallel noun phrases and avoid mixed wording like “messaging” vs. “planning”
- Consider adding one stronger systems-oriented phrase to reflect recent work: “Enterprise content operations” or “Digital governance for complex organizations”
- If space allows, combine two weaker items into one more senior-sounding line, e.g. “Public-sector advocacy communications and audience strategy”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” substantially repeat Core Competencies
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” is also echoed in the header and multiple NACo roles

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool dump and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. For a topline skills block, make it more strategic, grouped, and tied to the recent Drupal/CMS modernization work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability-led phrasing, e.g. “Drupal and enterprise CMS delivery” instead of just “Drupal.”
- Group related items and trim lower-priority terms: “Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages • CMS modernization and front-end implementation • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Consider replacing “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” with “front-end implementation (HTML/CSS/JavaScript)” for concision and a more senior tone.
- Put the strongest/recent themes first: Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, integrations/automation.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates much of “Technical + IT”; keep this section high-level and leave specific tools like jQuery/Airtable to the technical section.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also appears in Core Competencies; keep it here only if positioned as technical execution rather than strategy.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization

items.aiFeedback:

- If accurate, strengthen with scale language tied to recent work: “enterprise analytics infrastructure” or “reporting for high-traffic public-sector platforms”

- “SEO and performance analysis” is broad; consider “SEO and digital performance optimization” for cleaner phrasing

- Reframe toward scope and seniority: “Broadcast-quality multimedia production and hybrid event delivery”

items.title: University of Virginia

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic keyword dump and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This item should either be tightened to emphasize strongest/recent platforms or reframed to show level of use.

Suggested edit:
- Prioritize the most relevant/recent tools first: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, add proficiency context instead of just names: **Drupal (enterprise modernization, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Consider renaming the heading to be more specific: **CMS & Web Publishing Platforms**
- If Drupal is the clear differentiator from recent roles, visually weight it: **Drupal (primary) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This duplicates the “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” Topline Skills entry almost exactly; keep the fuller version in one place and make this one shorter or more platform-only.
- “CMS modernization” is already covered elsewhere, so don’t add that phrase here unless removing it from Topline Skills.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical coverage, but this reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools actually used in recent roles and group items more clearly.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: “Front-end implementation: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery”
- Add a second grouped phrase: “Technical tooling: API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions”
- Consider dropping version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless the rest of the CV uses that style; “HTML, CSS, JavaScript” is cleaner.
- If accurate, strengthen with scope/context instead of breadth alone, e.g. “Front-end implementation for Drupal-based public websites, campaign microsites and workflow integrations.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- “Workflow automation” appears elsewhere; avoid repeating adjacent concepts unless this section adds more specific tools or context.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item reads as an undifferentiated software list and overlaps with “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” elsewhere. Tighten it around actual automation/platform strengths and de-emphasize generic collaboration tools.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Tools**
- Reorder by relevance/strength: **Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Trello • Slack • Microsoft Teams • Basecamp**
- If accurate, add light qualifiers instead of a pure list, e.g.: **Airtable (workflow databases) • Power Automate, Zapier (process automation) • Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp (project/workflow management) • Slack, Microsoft Teams (team coordination)**
- Consider dropping 1–2 lowest-value/general tools unless they are used heavily; the strongest signals here are Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, and Asana.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Core Competencies/Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing verbatim.
- Slack/Teams are common workplace tools and may dilute impact unless this section is curated to emphasize systems you built or administered.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant tools, but this item is too bare compared with the rest of the CV and misses a chance to signal scale or use case. Since email leadership already appears strongly in recent NACo roles, keep this as a concise platform list rather than restating channel ownership.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten/standardize platform naming: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add a light qualifier to show practical depth without repeating work history, e.g. **campaign automation, newsletter operations, audience segmentation**
- Example final line: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp • Campaign automation • Newsletter operations • Audience segmentation**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid adding “email newsletters reaching tens of thousands” here; that impact is already better covered in recent work experience.
- Don’t repeat broad “multi-channel communications” language already covered in Core Competencies and role descriptions.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but the item is too broad and overlaps with the 2018–2024 NACo roles. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with concrete outputs rather than leadership language that belongs to later roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize early-career buildout: “Promoted across two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital media function, supporting web, email, social and multimedia production.”
- Add specific execution/results: mention number/frequency of livestreams, weekly video updates, or scope of website refresh if known.
- Tighten phrasing: replace “high-impact digital content” with named deliverables like “livestreamed events, weekly advocacy videos, and web content.”
- Recast supervision modestly: “coordinated day-to-day work with a digital media associate” unless formal management was part of the role.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Strengthening workflows” and “weekly video updates” overlap with the 2018–2022 role; keep this entry focused on building/producing, not leading operations.
- “Website refresh” may feel repetitive with the later 10,000+ page redesign; distinguish it as an earlier refresh, not enterprise modernization.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a credible “first podcast” achievement, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo digital/media roles. Emphasize the podcast launch and cross-functional coordination, and trim broad phrases like “supporting organizational programs and policy work.”

Suggested edit:
- Reframe around distinct contributions: “Coordinated innovation and applied research projects for county policy/program initiatives.”
- Make the standout achievement the lead clause: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting, and production.”
- Tighten multimedia language: replace “Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials” with “Produced digital and multimedia content to support program communications.”
- If possible, add scope or output metrics: number of projects supported, podcast episodes launched, audiences reached, or teams/stakeholders coordinated.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital content production and multimedia” overlaps with later Digital Media Manager/Producer and Associate Communications Director entries; keep this item focused on podcast launch and innovation/research coordination.
- Avoid overstating digital leadership here since stronger, more recent leadership evidence appears in 2018–2024 roles.
